summary:
The code does what the design said. `Kernel32.CriticalErrorBoxOff.Begin()` is the first statement of `SynchronousIoCancel.Open` (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:352). Its token goes to both CreateFile routes (:364, :367, :394). The CreateFileW import is private (Kernel32.cs:120) behind a wrapper that refuses a scope `Begin()` did not make (Kernel32.cs:106-117). TryGetVolumeUsed now uses the same scope, and a test hook inside that scope reads the mode (Kernel32.cs:170-187).

What I ran myself:
- The full default suite: 413 passed, 0 failed. The exact repro command: 1 passed, exit 0.
- Fitness check: all 62 rules hold. rules-parity -ExpectFacts 12: AGREE. RuleCases C-001: 'All checks held.'
- I read every new Fact against its matrix row, and each one feeds its shape in. The scan-thread `Created` seam is [ThreadStatic], so the nested-folder Fact counts only scan-thread opens. The nested-folder Fact really scans a\sub. The route Fact asserts KeptLastAccess true and false.

What the build got wrong: its claim that this machine has no removable drive is false. Right now E:\ and F:\ are Removable with IsReady=False, so they are empty removable drives. That was the reason case C-013 was deferred. I ran the built Core against both from a child process with inherited process mode 0x8003, so no box could appear. On each drive, OpenDirectory returned 21 with 0x1 set inside and 0x0 restored after, TryGetVolumeUsed returned false/21, and Scanner.Scan ended RootUnreadable with RootError 21. So the error half of the real bug is now shown on real hardware. The box half, the one thing this slice exists to fix, can now be checked end to end here, and no stage has done it.

One smaller gap is left from accepted finding M2. Kernel32.cs is excepted wholesale, and inside it the private CreateFileW and GetDiskFreeSpaceEx can be called with no scope. Yet the rule's own `because` says the compiler holds both excepted files.

This slice has not looped: one build attempt, and code-review attempt 1 never ran (provider session limit).

Second round: Second round, read as an attacker. The one new defect is in the matcher this diff adds. The PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen pattern matches only a call written with the Win32 name followed by `(`. That makes it blind to an import written in the repo's own style: `EntryPoint = "CreateFileW"` on a method with a different C# name, called by that name. It also misses the ANSI `...A` variants and exports looked up by name.

I ran the exact pattern through .NET Regex on those inputs, and all four returned match=False:
- a `[LibraryImport(..., EntryPoint = "CreateFileW")] ... OpenPath(...)` declaration and its `Win.OpenPath(path, ...)` call
- `Win.CreateFileA(`
- `Ntdll.NtQueryAttributesFile(`
- `NativeLibrary.GetExport(k32, "CreateFileW")`

The controls, a CRLF between name and `(` and a plain `GetFileAttributesExW(`, matched as they should. The repo does write imports this way: Kernel32.cs:133 (GetVolumeInformationByHandleW), Kernel32.cs:250 (GetDiskFreeSpaceExW) and Monitors.cs:19 (GetMonitorInfoW) all use EntryPoint with a different C# name. The old CreateFile import matched only because its C# name happened to equal the Win32 name minus the W.

Other boundaries I walked found nothing new:
- Enter throwing, the wrapper throwing, AfterCall throwing and a refused Enter all unwind through the `using` in Open.
- Scope Dispose runs after LastError() has been read, and no caller reads the last error after Open returns.
- A failed Begin gives an armed scope that restores nothing.
- CRLF, BOM and comment handling in the regex agree between the Fact and Fitness.
- The yaml quoting (`''`) is valid.
- The plants.json row count (42) adds up.

The disposed-scope and cross-thread token holes can only be reached inside the two excepted files, which round 1's m1 already covers. Round-1 findings, obligations and cases stand as filed; nothing here changes them.

findings.claim: Case C-013 (open a drive with no media: ERROR_NOT_READY 21 goes into Open's failure path) was deferred as non-material because 'No engine stage can produce an empty removable drive'. The build repeated this as 'this machine has no removable drive (drives are C: fixed, D: fixed, Z: network)'. That no longer holds on this machine, and possibly never did (Get-Volume, for one, lists no empty card-reader slots). `[System.IO.DriveInfo]::GetDrives()` reports `E:\ Removable` and `F:\ Removable`, both IsReady=False: two empty removable drives, exactly the bug's shape. The slice's whole acceptance rests on a proxy, the thread mode sampled at AfterCall, on the stated grounds that validate cannot reach such a drive. Validate can reach one now, and nobody has watched the reported symptom (the 'insert a disk' box) stay away on a real empty drive. I exercised the error half from a child process whose process mode was 0x8003, so it could not tell box from no box. Built Core on E: and F: gave: OpenDirectory error=21, modeInside=1, threadAfter=0x0; TryGetVolumeUsed ok=False error=21; Scanner.Scan status=RootUnreadable rootError=21. This confirms the overridden m5 reasoning end to end, but not the box.
findings.evidence: Design case 'open a drive with no media ... material: false', with the why 'No engine stage can produce an empty removable drive'. Build LEFT OPEN: 'No end-to-end test on a removable drive with no media (design case C-013...). No stage here can produce one'. Build command account for read-window: 'this machine has no removable drive'. Measured here: DriveInfo shows E:\ and F:\ Removable, IsReady=False. A reflection run of src/FsAnalyser.Core/bin/Debug/net10.0-windows/FsAnalyser.Core.dll under pwsh (.NET 10.0.12, child process mode 0x8003) produced the numbers above.
findings.fix: At validate-slice, first confirm E:\ (or F:\) still has IsReady=False. Then run the published FsAnalyser.App.exe against it, launched so the child process's error mode lacks 0x1: CreateProcess with CREATE_DEFAULT_ERROR_MODE, or the spike's explorer.exe launch, which measured 0x0. Record that mode, and confirm the report shows RootUnreadable with error 21 and that no hard-error box appeared. Optionally, also add an opt-in Fact in FailCriticalErrorsTests that scans an empty removable drive when one is present and asserts RootUnreadable/21 with 0x1 at AfterCall call 1.

findings.claim: The new rule's `because` in .taad/fitness.yaml, and the doc comment on its Fact, both say 'Kernel32.CreateFile takes the scope as an argument, so the compiler holds the two excepted files'. The build's O-017 claim also says 'no CreateFile call in any file compiles without a scope'. That is true of SynchronousIoCancel.cs, but not of Kernel32.cs. Inside Kernel32 the private `CreateFileW` (Kernel32.cs:120) and `GetDiskFreeSpaceEx` (Kernel32.cs:252) can be called by any member with no CriticalErrorBoxOff. Kernel32.cs is excepted wholesale from PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen, and it is where every new import naturally lands. So a new Kernel32 convenience method whose name is not in the alternation, say `Kernel32.TryReadAttributes(path)` wrapping CreateFileW or GetFileAttributesExW, passes the compiler, the xUnit Fact and Fitness, and opens a path with the box on. That is the second change shape accepted finding M2 named ('a new Kernel32 convenience method that opens a path'). Today's tree is correct; the rule text claims a guarantee that one of its excepted files does not have.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml, PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen because: '...so the compiler holds the two excepted files'. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:158-163, same sentence. src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/Kernel32.cs:119-122 (private CreateFileW), :250-253 (private GetDiskFreeSpaceEx). Neither the compiler nor the rule restricts their call sites within Kernel32.cs.
findings.fix: Add one assertion outside the twinned architecture Facts, so rules-parity counts do not move. For example, a Fact in FailCriticalErrorsTests that counts the call sites in Kernel32.cs: exactly one `CreateFileW(` call (inside CreateFile) and one `GetDiskFreeSpaceEx(` call (inside TryGetVolumeUsed), besides their declarations. Or, at the least, reword the `because` and the Fact doc to say the compiler holds SynchronousIoCancel.cs, and that Kernel32.cs is held only by review.

findings.claim: The widened must_not_match pattern `\b(CreateFile(W|2)?|...|GetDiskFreeSpace(Ex)?W?)\s*\(` requires the Win32 function name itself to appear followed by `(`. That misses the repo's own import idiom. A new Native file (allowed by InteropLivesOnlyInNative) that declares `[LibraryImport("kernel32.dll", EntryPoint = "CreateFileW")] internal static partial SafeFileHandle OpenPath(...)` and is called as `Win.OpenPath(path, ...)` from Scanning matches nowhere: the name sits in a string followed by `"`, and the method and call carry a different name. That opens a path with the critical-error box on, and passes the compiler, the xUnit Fact and Fitness. This is the change review m2 widened the rule to catch ('A new Native/Ntdll.cs would satisfy InteropLivesOnlyInNative and this rule at the same time'). Plant F25 only proves the naive form, where the method is named NtOpenFile. The ANSI variants (CreateFileA, FindFirstFileExA, GetFileAttributesExA, GetDiskFreeSpaceExA), NtQueryAttributesFile and NativeLibrary.GetExport(..., "CreateFileW") escape the same way. I ran the pattern on these inputs with .NET Regex (Multiline): all returned False, and the controls returned True.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml, entry 'PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen (*.cs)', must_not_match. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:165-171 has the same pattern. The repo writes renamed-import declarations at src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/Kernel32.cs:133 (EntryPoint = "GetVolumeInformationByHandleW" on GetVolumeInformationByHandle), Kernel32.cs:250 (EntryPoint = "GetDiskFreeSpaceExW" on GetDiskFreeSpaceEx) and Monitors.cs:19 (EntryPoint = "GetMonitorInfoW"). eng/rules-harness/plants.json F25 plants `NtOpenFile(` by its own name only.
findings.fix: In both the yaml entry and the xUnit Fact, allow `[AW]?` in place of `W?` in the call alternation. Then add a second pattern that matches the entry-point name as a string literal: `"(CreateFile[AW2]?|OpenFileById|Nt(Create|Open)File|Zw(Create|Open)File|NtQuery(Full)?AttributesFile|FindFirstFile(Ex)?[AW]?|GetFileAttributes(Ex)?[AW]?|GetVolumeInformation[AW]?|GetDiskFreeSpace(Ex)?[AW]?)"`. Kernel32.cs stays excepted, so its own EntryPoint strings do not fire. Add a plants.json row F26 that plants a new Native file declaring `EntryPoint = "CreateFileW"` on a renamed method, expected to fire in both engines. Then re-run rules-parity (pattern count 28 goes to 29, derived by RuleCases) and the harness.

obligations.evidence: I ran the exact command: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FailCriticalErrorsTests.TheScannersRootOpenAndSizeProbeRunWithTheCriticalErrorBoxOff"`, which gave Passed 1, exit 0. The fix that turns it green is at SynchronousIoCancel.cs:352, where the scope is the first statement of Open.

The scope is a `using` declaration over a readonly struct at SynchronousIoCancel.cs:352 and Kernel32.cs:170. Dispose restores `_previous` only when the set succeeded (Kernel32.cs:226-230). FailCriticalErrorsTests.NestedScopesUnwindInOrder asserts [1,1,1,2]. The preset Theory, AFailedOpen and ACancelledOrThrowing (refused, cancelled and throwing exits) and the dedicated-thread Fact each assert the preset comes back. All passed in my full run (413/413). The real empty-drive run also restored 0x0 after error 21.

The scope is outermost in Open (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:352), with one set/restore pair per open. The wrapper takes a token and arms no second scope (Kernel32.cs:106-117). The builder's 37 ns/pair figure came from a scratch Fact it deleted; I did not re-measure it.
FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs:34-75: a whole-tree scan of a temp tree, with rootMode read at the scan-thread guard's call 1 (the Created seam is [ThreadStatic], SynchronousIoCancel.cs:62-63). Passes.

The repro Fact hooks the probe worker's own guard through ScanOptions.Probe (:44-48). AProbeOnThisThreadOpensWithTheBoxOffAndGivesTheModeBack (:171-199) calls SizeProbe.Probe directly on the test thread and asserts modes[0]==0x1.

EveryFolderTheScanOpensIsOpenedWithTheBoxOff (:97-125) builds a\sub, a folder that holds a subfolder, and asserts Folders==2 and exactly four 0x1 calls, the first being call 1. With only the root guarded the count would be 2, so the Fact discriminates.

BothRoutesOfAFolderOpenRunWithTheBoxOff (:132-164) asserts KeptLastAccess true for the TryOpenKeepingLastAccess route and false where FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES is denied (fallback at :367), each with 0x1 at AfterCall and 0x2 restored. TryOpenKeepingLastAccess is private and has one caller (:364).
Theory InlineData(0u) at FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs:172 asserts after==preset.
Theory InlineData(NoGpFaultErrorBox=0x2) at :173 asserts the open sees exactly 0x1 and 0x2 is back after.
Theory InlineData(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) at :174, plus NestedScopesUnwindInOrder (:453-475).

AFailedOpenRanWithTheBoxOffAndGivesTheModeBack (:259-307): a folder denying FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY (error 5), a missing folder and a missing file, each with 0x1 inside and 0x2 after. A full scan records the denied folder as unreadable.

ACancelledOrThrowingOpenGivesTheModeBack (:314-377) covers three exits. Cancel issued inside call 1 of a real scan gives a Cancelled status. BeforeCall cancels, so Enter refuses and Open returns Aborted; Begin runs before Enter, so the mode is 0x1 there. AfterCall throws PlantedFailure. Each restores 0x2.

Built in the form review m3 accepted: ProbesOnSeveralThreadsAtOnceEachGiveTheirThreadItsModeBack (:206-252) runs 4 dedicated threads at a Barrier, 2 probes each, with half preset to 0x2, and checks the baseline after each probe. No Fact depends on which pool thread runs next.

TheVolumeReadRunsWithTheBoxOffAndGivesTheModeBack (:384-415) uses the %TEMP% drive root and a free letter from GetLogicalDrives, which includes E:/F:, so it picks Y:. BeforeVolumeRead reads [1,1] inside the scope, and 0x2 is back after each call. My real run on the empty E:/F: also returned false/21.
My full default-suite run passed 413/413. It includes the counting-rule classes (LinkTests, HardlinkTests, OnDiskSizeTests, LongPathTests, UnreadableFolderTests), which are unchanged by this diff.

Kernel32.cs:206-209 declares the parameterless ctor [Obsolete(error: true)]. The real ctor is private (:211). IsArmed is false for default (:219), and CreateFile throws on an unarmed scope (:108-115). The BeforeVolumeRead hook sits inside the scope (:170-171, :186-187). AScopeNotMadeByBeginTurnsNothingOffAndOpensNothing and the volume Fact pass. I did not re-run the builder's mutation, but the volume Fact's [1,1] against a 0x2 preset would fail with an unarmed scope by construction.

CreateFileW is private (Kernel32.cs:119-122), and the only entry point is CreateFile(in CriticalErrorBoxOff, ...) (:106). Open keeps its `using` and passes the token to both routes (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:364, 367, 394). Residual gap: calls inside Kernel32.cs itself are not held; see finding m1.

The .taad/fitness.yaml twinned entry 'PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen (*.cs)', the ArchitectureRulesTests.PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen Fact (:165-171) and plants.json F24, F25 and P24 are all present. I ran rules-parity -ExpectFacts 12 (AGREE: 12 facts, 16 twinned, 28 patterns) and RuleCases C-001 ('All checks held'). I did not re-run the rules harness, which needs the engine's backend path; its 55/55 AS-RECORDED is the builder's figure.

The yaml pattern and the Fact's pattern are the same widened alternation, (CreateFile(W|2)?|OpenFileById|NtCreateFile|NtOpenFile|ZwCreateFile|ZwOpenFile|FindFirstFile(Ex)?W?|GetFileAttributes(Ex)?W?|GetVolumeInformationW?|GetDiskFreeSpace(Ex)?W?), and parity agrees. A Fitness check over the tree holds with no hits.
No Fact depends on pool-thread reuse. The dedicated-thread Fact is at :206-252, and the deterministic preset, failed and cancelled Facts are kept.
BothRoutes asserts KeptLastAccess for each of two fixtures (keeping and refusing), together with the 0x1 sample (:162-163).

The code keeps one pair per open (the token is not nested; Kernel32.cs:106-117). The timing (37 ns/pair against 15.8 µs/open) is builder-reported from a deleted scratch Fact, so there is nothing to check in the tree. would_force_resynthesis in the design record is still true, as the builder noted.

cases.evidence: FailCriticalErrorsTests.TheScannersRootOpenAndSizeProbeRunWithTheCriticalErrorBoxOff: scans a temp tree and samples the scan-thread guard's call 1 (the root open) through the [ThreadStatic] Created seam.
Repro Fact: the ScanOptions.Probe wrapper hooks the worker's own guard on the probe worker thread. The AProbeOnThisThread Theory calls SizeProbe.Probe directly on the test thread.
EveryFolderTheScanOpensIsOpenedWithTheBoxOff: the tree holds a\sub\c.bin, so 'a' is a folder containing a subfolder. It asserts four box-off opens, of the root twice, a, and a\sub.
BothRoutesOfAFolderOpenRunWithTheBoxOff: KeptLastAccess==true proves the TryOpenKeepingLastAccess route ran. Denying FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES forces the fallback CreateFile (KeptLastAccess==false).
AProbeOnThisThread Theory with InlineData(0u): the thread is preset to 0 and the mode is read after Probe.
The same Theory with InlineData(0x2): the open reads exactly 0x1 and 0x2 is back after.
The same Theory with InlineData(0x1), plus NestedScopesUnwindInOrder, where the inner scope gives back the outer scope's 0x1.

AFailedOpenRanWithTheBoxOffAndGivesTheModeBack: a folder with FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY denied (error 5 on both routes), a missing folder and a missing file. It also runs a full scan of the tree holding the denied folder.

ACancelledOrThrowingOpenGivesTheModeBack: cancel is issued inside the root open's bracket through Scans.CancelDuringTheCall, so Open returns Aborted through Settle and the scan ends Cancelled. It also covers a refusal from BeforeCall and a throw from AfterCall.

The shape as written, pool-thread reuse, was replaced as review m3 accepted by ProbesOnSeveralThreadsAtOnceEachGiveTheirThreadItsModeBack. It runs 4 dedicated threads concurrently at a Barrier, 2 probes each, and each thread checks its own baseline after each probe.
TheVolumeReadRunsWithTheBoxOffAndGivesTheModeBack: the %TEMP% drive root plus a free drive letter, with 0x1 read inside the scope through the BeforeVolumeRead hook and 0x2 restored.
The counting-rule classes are unchanged and passed within my full default-suite run (413/413) through the guarded Open.

No test feeds an empty removable drive. The deferral reason ('no engine stage can produce an empty removable drive') is false here: E:\ and F:\ are Removable with IsReady=False. My hand run of the built Core gave error 21, RootUnreadable/21 and a restored mode, but under process mode 0x8003, so it cannot tell box from no box. See finding M1.
Out of scope by design (non-material, an open question to a person). Pulling media mid-scan still needs a person, so that deferral reason still holds.

drift: Every departure from the design was declared by the build: factory `Kernel32.CriticalErrorBoxOff.Begin()` instead of `TurnOffCriticalErrorBox()`, with the parameterless ctor made [Obsolete(error:true)]; the wrapper keeps the name `Kernel32.CreateFile`; the rule is renamed from the design's prose name to 'PathOpensGoOnlyThroughTheGuardedOpen (*.cs)' and turned into a twinned entry, with the engine-added '# settled by SL-077' block removed.

The rule rename matters at merge. If the engine re-adds a '# settled by SL-077' block under the design's prose name, the rule is held twice (the HF-008 shape), and plants F24 and F25 would need also_settled.

The build's environment claim 'this machine has no removable drive (drives are C: fixed, D: fixed, Z: network)' is false now. E:\ and F:\ are Removable with IsReady=False, which DriveInfo reports and Get-Volume does not. Every stage's premise that 'validate cannot reach an empty removable drive', including the slice's own statement, is wrong for this machine as it stands.

The design record still has would_force_resynthesis: true on the per-open cost question, and its key_decision still rejects a process-wide call on race and App-interop grounds. The accepted dispositions for m1 and m6 say both should be restated. That is a design-record edit, not code.
A test-only [ThreadStatic] hook, `Kernel32.BeforeVolumeRead`, now sits in production Kernel32. The M1 disposition asked for it, and it matches the existing AfterCall/BeforeCall/Created seams.
unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-077/design-slice-1.json, critique-1.json, critique-review-1.json, build-slice-1.json: stage records, not code. Their content reached me in the brief, and I read only index.json.
